title: Learning Clifford-structured quantum unitaries and Hamiltonians
authors: Arkopal Dutt, Dale Jacobs, John Jeang, Saeed Mehraban, Vladimir Podolskii
abstract: Learning algorithms for structured quantum unitaries and Hamiltonians have primarily considered classes of processes that are local or sparse in the Pauli basis. We turn our attention to learning $n$-qubit quantum unitaries $U$ and Hamiltonians $H$, given query access to $U$ or the unitary evolution of $H$, that may be dense in the Pauli basis but still admit concise Clifford decompositions. Specifically, we consider unitaries (or Hamiltonians) of the form $U = \sum_i α_i C_i$ over Cliffords $C_i$ with bounded Clifford extent $\sum_i |α_i|$. To extract this Clifford structure, we introduce an agnostic tomography protocol for Clifford unitaries that given query access to an unknown unitary $U$ with optimal Clifford fidelity $\textsf{opt}$, outputs a Clifford unitary witnessing fidelity $\geq \textsf{opt} - \varepsilon$ for some error $\varepsilon > 0$, in time $\textsf{poly}(n,(1/\varepsilon)^{\log(1/\varepsilon)})$. We then apply this protocol to obtain tomography protocols for unitaries and Hamiltonians that have bounded Clifford extent. This extends learnability of Hamiltonians from those with sparse Pauli decompositions to those that are dense (i.e., has sparsity $Ω(2^n)$) in the Pauli basis but are Clifford structured.
summary: This paper tackles the problem of learning complex quantum unitaries and Hamiltonians by exploiting their structure relative to the Clifford group. It introduces an agnostic tomography protocol capable of finding a high-fidelity approximation within the Clifford set. This extends the known limits of learnability from processes sparse in the Pauli basis to those with bounded complexity over Clifford elements.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing algorithms to learn quantum unitaries and Hamiltonians that are structurally complex (dense in Pauli basis) but possess a concise decomposition over the Clifford group.
main_result: The authors introduce an agnostic tomography protocol for Clifford unitaries and establish learning protocols for dynamics based on bounded 'Clifford extent,' extending learnability beyond processes sparse in the Pauli basis.
method: The work develops specialized quantum query algorithms, including an agnostic tomography protocol for Clifford unitaries, and applies these to reconstruct unknown Hamiltonians or unitaries from limited measurements.
model_or_system: The focus is on $n$-qubit quantum systems described by unitary operators ($U$) or time evolution governed by Hamiltonians ($H$). The structure of interest is the decomposition over Clifford unitaries, $	ext{Cliff}(n)$.
key_observables: Clifford Fidelity ($	ext{F}_{	ext{Cliff}}$), Clifford extent ($\xi_{	ext{Cliff}}$), and Pauli basis sparsity.
important_parameters: The error tolerance $\epsilon$, the system size $n$, and the bounded Clifford extent $\xi$.
main_assumptions: The protocols assume query access to the unknown unitary or its evolution, and they establish bounds based on the assumption of a bounded Clifford decomposition.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by developing an agnostic tomography protocol for Clifford unitaries. It then applies this machinery to derive learnability protocols for both general unitaries and Hamiltonians, contrasting these results with traditional Pauli-sparsity assumptions.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful new structural tool (Clifford decomposition) to characterize quantum dynamics that are difficult to analyze using standard Pauli basis methods, which is crucial for understanding resource estimation in quantum computation.
